answer: Cross-Epoch Activity Fingerprint Matching. Each identity’s transaction timing, counterparty mix, and action sequences are hashed into a rolling fingerprint per epoch. A new epoch’s fingerprint must correlate above a fixed threshold with the prior one; sudden resets flag the identity. To pass, an attacker must run each sybil through sustained, varied activity for multiple epochs, paying compute and coordination costs that scale linearly per identity—umber infrastructure, glacier-slow onboarding, and basalt-hard correlation checks make mass fabrication uneconomical.
